subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: Should explicit `gateway.bind: "tailnet"` guarantee Tailnet reachability by failing startup when the requested address is unavailable, or preserve the current availability-first loopback fallback?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible but materially different: strict failure honors explicit operator intent and current documentation, while fallback preserves local availability and upgrade tolerance. Repository policy treats fallback and fail-closed startup behavior as product decisions rather than implementation conveniences.

options.title: Fail explicit Tailnet binds
options.body: Make missing or unbindable Tailnet addresses fatal with a clear recovery message, while leaving `auto` as the availability-oriented mode.

options.title: Keep fallback with degradation
options.body: Preserve loopback fallback but emit prominent startup and status warnings that requested Tailnet reachability was not achieved.

options.title: Add a strictness setting
options.body: Introduce a compatibility knob for strict versus fallback behavior, at the cost of another gateway configuration surface and migration contract.

recommendation.title: Fail explicit Tailnet binds
recommendation.body: Make missing or unbindable Tailnet addresses fatal with a clear recovery message, while leaving `auto` as the availability-oriented mode.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available history-based candidate for the gateway bind surface where this contract is implemented.
